## Summary

Add `server/src/swole/coacheval/artifacts.py` (the frozen `RunArtifacts` dataclass, `capture()`,
`save()`, `load()`) and `server/src/swole/coacheval/exemplar.py` (`apply_exemplar()`) per
[plan §5](https://github.com/Senkichi/swole/blob/599e6fd0c5a5c1208d6426f6373470c3d5900fd5/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-evidence-coach-remaining-issues.md#5-interface-contracts-shared-across-issues).
`capture()` turns the `EvalTree` #275 produces plus a post-run coach tree into a
`RunArtifacts`: the new journal entry, the working-tree diff, and what the server's own release
gates say about the tree — all found relative to `tree.base_sha`, never the tree's current git
`HEAD`, because a real coach run ends in `swole release`, which commits. `apply_exemplar()` is
the offline stand-in for that real run: it writes a hand-authored `journal.md` as the newest
entry and layers an optional `coach/` overlay onto the tree, with no model call and no commit.

## Why

[Spec — Eval harness](https://github.com/Senkichi/swole/blob/599e6fd0c5a5c1208d6426f6373470c3d5900fd5/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-evidence-coach-design.md#eval-harness)
calls for a runner that "captures the journal entry" after a coach run and scores it. Decision E3
([plan §4](https://github.com/Senkichi/swole/blob/599e6fd0c5a5c1208d6426f6373470c3d5900fd5/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-evidence-coach-remaining-issues.md#4-decisions-made-here-and-deviations-from-the-spec))
is what makes that testable in CI without a model: every scenario ships a `pass/` and one
`fail-<dimension>/` exemplar, and pytest proves the pass exemplar passes and each fail exemplar
fails on exactly that dimension. `apply_exemplar` is the one function that turns a static exemplar
directory into something `capture()` can process exactly as if a real coach run had produced it.

## Fix shape

**`server/src/swole/coacheval/artifacts.py`** (new):

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunArtifacts:
    scenario_id: str
    run_index: int
    coach_dir: Path
    base_sha: str
    journal_entry: str | None
    coach_diff: str
    release_errors: tuple[str, ...]
    timed_out: bool
    error: str | None
    model: str | None
    usage: dict | None


def journal_entries_at(coach_dir: Path, rev: str) -> list[tuple[tuple[int, int], str]]:
    """[(week, body)] parsed at an explicit git rev — NOT `prevstate.
    _load_head_journal_entries` (prevstate.py:345), which hardcodes the
    literal ref "HEAD:JOURNAL.md" and would read the WRONG state once a
    real coach run's `swole release` has committed past `rev`. Same
    `_HEADING` split as `coachbrief._journal_entries` (coachbrief.py:896)."""
    from ..coachbrief import _HEADING
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "show", f"{rev}:JOURNAL.md"], cwd=coach_dir,
        capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return []
    entries: list[tuple[tuple[int, int], list[str]]] = []
    for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
        m = _HEADING.match(line)
        if m:
            entries.append(((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))), []))
        elif entries:
            entries[-1][1].append(line)
    return [(wk, "\n".join(body)) for wk, body in entries]


def _gate_errors(tree: EvalTree) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The release gates' verdict on the run's WHOLE change, relative to
    base_sha. The gates read the literal HEAD (prevstate.load_head_state),
    and a live run ends in `swole release`, which commits — so HEAD is moved
    back to base_sha for the dry run and restored afterwards. A soft reset
    touches neither the index nor the working tree."""
    from ..coachrepo import CoachRepo, CoachValidationError

    head = _git(tree.coach_dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
    moved = head != tree.base_sha
    if moved:
        _git(tree.coach_dir, "reset", "--soft", tree.base_sha)
    try:
        CoachRepo(tree.coach_dir, tree.exercise_dir).release(
            "coach-eval: dry-run gate check", dry_run=True
        )
        return ()
    except CoachValidationError as e:
        return tuple(e.errors)
    finally:
        if moved:
            _git(tree.coach_dir, "reset", "--soft", head)


def capture(tree: EvalTree, *, scenario_id: str, run_index: int, **run_facts) -> RunArtifacts:
    from ..bakeoff.artifacts import coach_diff
    from ..journalgate import parse_new_run_entry

    head_entries = journal_entries_at(tree.coach_dir, tree.base_sha)
    run_entry = parse_new_run_entry(tree.coach_dir / "JOURNAL.md", head_entries)

    release_errors = _gate_errors(tree)

    return RunArtifacts(
        scenario_id=scenario_id, run_index=run_index, coach_dir=tree.coach_dir,
        base_sha=tree.base_sha, journal_entry=run_entry.body if run_entry else None,
        coach_diff=coach_diff(tree.coach_dir, tree.base_sha), release_errors=release_errors,
        **run_facts,  # timed_out, error, model, usage — caller-supplied; offline callers pass False/None/None/None
    )
```

`CoachRepo.release(message, dry_run=True)` (coachrepo.py:632-787, gate region coachrepo.py:654-713)
runs `load()` plus every release-time gate and writes nothing; `CoachValidationError.errors:
list[str]` (coachrepo.py:44-47) is the exact list `release()` would otherwise raise.

**Trap — the gates read the literal `HEAD`.** `release()`'s own `load_head_state` call is pinned
to `"HEAD"` (coachrepo.py:669-684). On the offline path `HEAD` never moves past `base_sha`, so a
plain dry run is right. A live run (#280) has already committed through `swole release` by
the time `capture()` runs, and a dry run against that tree would read the run's own commit as
history, find no new journal entry, and skip the journal and evidence gates without a word —
`release_errors == ()` for a run that may have committed around the gates with a raw
`git commit`. `_gate_errors` above closes that at the source rather than leaving it to each
caller: it moves `HEAD` back to `base_sha` with `git reset --soft`, runs the dry run, and restores
`HEAD` in a `finally`. A soft reset leaves the index and the working tree alone, so the gates see
the run's whole change as uncommitted work, exactly as they do offline; `release()` has no gate
on the `REVISION` file itself (coachrepo.py:776-780 only writes it), so the bumped value in the
working tree is inert. `tree.coach_dir` is always a throwaway — a materialised temp tree or a
sandbox clone, never the live `coach/` — which is what makes moving its `HEAD` acceptable.
`_git(cwd, *args) -> str` is a module-local helper (`subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd,
check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8").stdout.strip()`), the same shape
#275's `materialise` uses.

`save(artifacts, run_dir)` / `load(run_dir)` — `save` first copies the tree,
`shutil.copytree(artifacts.coach_dir, run_dir / "coach", dirs_exist_ok=True)`, `.git` included so
`coach_diff`/`must_not` re-checks need no model on rescore, and only then writes
`run_dir/artifacts.json` (every field except `coach_dir`, replaced with the literal `"coach"`)
through a sibling temp file and `os.replace`. **The order is a contract:** `artifacts.json` is
the last write of a run, so its presence means the run directory is complete — #280's
resume logic treats a run directory without one as half-written and repeats it. `load` reverses
both steps, setting `coach_dir=run_dir / "coach"`. Trap: on Windows, copying an open git repo's `.git`
directory can hit a locked pack/index file if any subprocess against `coach_dir` is still alive —
close every `subprocess.run` handle before `save()` runs (matching the `contextlib.closing`
discipline `coachrepo.py:736` already uses for the same class of Windows file-lock issue).

**`server/src/swole/coacheval/exemplar.py`** (new):

```python
def apply_exemplar(tree: EvalTree, exemplar_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Offline stand-in for a real coach run (E3): appends the exemplar's
    journal.md as the newest JOURNAL.md entry and layers its optional
    coach/ overlay onto the tree. No commit, no model call — tree.base_sha
    stays the pre-exemplar HEAD, so capture()'s journal_entries_at(...,
    tree.base_sha) sees the appended entry as new."""
    overlay = exemplar_dir / "coach"
    if overlay.is_dir():
        assert not (overlay / "JOURNAL.md").exists(), (
            "the overlay supplies rules.yaml/evidence/templates changes only —"
            " the new entry itself comes from journal.md, appended below"
        )
        shutil.copytree(overlay, tree.coach_dir, dirs_exist_ok=True)

    journal_path = tree.coach_dir / "JOURNAL.md"
    existing = journal_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if journal_path.exists() else ""
    new_entry = (exemplar_dir / "journal.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    sep = "" if not existing else ("\n" if existing.endswith("\n") else "\n\n")
    journal_path.write_text(existing + sep + new_entry, encoding="utf-8")
```

Design decision this issue is making, since no exemplar fixtures exist yet to copy the shape
from: `journal.md` carries the FULL new entry text, including its own `## YYYY-Www` heading and
a line-anchored `SESSION RUN <id>` (or `IDLE RUN <date>` for an `idle`-trigger scenario) marker —
`journalgate.parse_new_run_entry` (journalgate.py:410) returns `None` outright when no such
marker is present (journalgate.py:439-443), so a marker-less exemplar produces no capturable
`journal_entry` at all. `_HEADING`'s parse (`^## (\d{4})-W(\d{2})\b`) does not require blank-line
separation between entries, so the appended-entry separator above is cosmetic only.

**Tests** (`server/tests/test_coacheval_artifacts.py`), each against a real `CoachRepo.init_repo()`
git tree under `tmp_path` (never a mocked git):

- `test_capture_finds_new_entry_relative_to_base_sha_not_head` — the regression case: commit the
  exemplar's journal entry onto the tree (simulating that `swole release` already ran) so `HEAD`
  has moved past `tree.base_sha`, then assert `capture().journal_entry` still returns the new
  entry's body instead of `None`.
- `test_capture_release_errors_survive_a_committed_run` — apply a gate-violating exemplar, commit
  it with a raw `git commit` so `HEAD` moves past `tree.base_sha`, then assert
  `capture().release_errors` still carries the gate's message and that `git rev-parse HEAD` is
  the same commit after `capture()` as before it.
- `test_save_writes_artifacts_json_last` — with `shutil.copytree` patched to raise, no
  `artifacts.json` exists afterwards.
- `test_capture_release_errors_empty_on_a_clean_exemplar`
- `test_capture_release_errors_nonempty_on_a_broken_exemplar` — a journal body missing the
  `Hypotheses:` block, asserting the same message `CoachValidationError` would raise.
- `test_coach_diff_reflects_both_committed_and_uncommitted_changes`
- `test_save_load_round_trip_preserves_every_field_and_the_coach_tree_git_history`
- `test_apply_exemplar_produces_a_capturable_run_entry` — end to end: `materialise()` an
  `EvalTree`, `apply_exemplar()` a `pass/` fixture into it, `capture()` it, assert
  `journal_entry` is non-`None` and contains the fixture's own hypothesis text.
- `test_apply_exemplar_rejects_an_overlay_that_carries_its_own_journal`
- `test_apply_exemplar_is_a_noop_overlay_when_coach_fixture_dir_is_absent`

## Acceptance

- `server/tests/test_coacheval_artifacts.py::test_capture_finds_new_entry_relative_to_base_sha_not_head` passes — this is the wired proof that `capture()` calls `journal_entries_at(..., tree.base_sha)`, not any HEAD-pinned reader.
- `server/tests/test_coacheval_artifacts.py::test_capture_release_errors_survive_a_committed_run` passes — the same invariant for the gate verdict: a committed run cannot hide from the release gates.
- `server/tests/test_coacheval_artifacts.py::test_apply_exemplar_produces_a_capturable_run_entry` passes — proves `apply_exemplar()` and `capture()` compose into one real, model-free coach-run stand-in.
- `uv run pytest -q --tb=short` green for the whole `server/` suite.
- `uv run ruff check . ; uv run ruff format --check .` clean.
